extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, regulators (EPA/CARB), Volkswagen executives, dealers, affected customers, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a U.S. House congressional oversight hearing questioning Volkswagen executives about defeat devices, remediation plans, timelines, dealer/customer impacts, and regulatory interactions. The document records legislators' criteria for evaluating VW's responses and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for remedy development and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is responsible for developing and testing the solution to remedy the defeat devices?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility lies within the Engine and Drivetrain Division in Germany, in Wolfsburg, for engine and drivetrain software for the two-cylinder and the four-cylinder TDI engines. (Mr. Horn: "The responsibility for developing and testing the engine and drivetrain software lies within the Engine and Drivetrain Division in Germany, in Wolfsburg...")

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether fixes require software-only or hardware changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish whether the remedy can be a software patch or will require changes to vehicle architecture and hardware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generation distinctions: ~430,000 Gen 1 vehicles likely cannot be fixed by software-only and require hardware (e.g., additional NOx catalytic converter or SCR Urea Tank) plus software; Gen 2 (Passat) likely software; Gen 3 to be addressed separately. Hardware engineering is complex and takes time. (Quotes about software-only solution not being possible for Gen 1 and listing hardware options.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely coordination with regulators (EPA and CARB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate proposed fixes, testing, and timelines with the EPA and California Air Resources Board (CARB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW must discuss and test proposed solutions with agencies in a timely manner — e.g., Gen 2 solutions 'being discussed in a timely manner now in the next couple of weeks with the California Air Resources Board and the CARB.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and truthfulness of representations to regulators and public
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations made to regulators (EPA/CARB) about causes of increased emissions must be truthful and corrected when false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW initially told EPA and CARB that increased emissions were due to technical issues and unexpected in-use conditions; those representations were later admitted to be incorrect/false. (Ms. DeGette: "Those representations ... were, in fact, incorrect and false, weren’t they, sir?" Mr. Horn: "Yes.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal investigation and disclosure of who knew when
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct investigations to determine who within the company knew about the defeat device and when, and disclose findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations ongoing; Jones Day retained to investigate 'who did what, when, how, and why.' Executives questioned on whether they knew of activity in 2014 vs. learning about it on Sept 3, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness verification of prior recall fixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether previously proposed or implemented recall fixes actually resolved the emissions discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CARB reported that earlier recall fixes (December 2014) did not work. Queries over whether VW's recalled vehicles passed follow-up evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, timely communication to dealers and customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide dealers and customers with up-to-date information, FAQs, guidance, and direct communication about the issue and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW has issued dealer calls, videos, letters, and FAQs; call centers and dealers must receive the same real-time information. Dealers should be guided on contacting customers and handling inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealer financial relief and mitigation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer remedies to dealers to mitigate inventory, cashflow, and bonus/incentive disruptions caused by inability to sell affected vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures described include free flooring for TDIs/used/new cars, removal of bonus thresholds (maximum bonus paid), discretionary funds wired to dealers, increased incentives (e.g., $1,000–$1,500 per car or other amounts), and other cashflow support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer remedies and compensation if performance/fuel economy affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and provide compensation to vehicle owners if remediation negatively affects fuel economy, engine performance, or vehicle value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fixes change performance or MPG (Monroney label), VW will discuss compensating customers. Loss-in-value calculations and scenarios are being developed; customers expect to be made whole if significant differences occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent timeline and schedule for technical fixes and recalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear timetable for when software fixes and hardware remedies will be developed, approved by agencies, and rolled out to vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW indicated different timing by generation: Gen 3 may be later; Gen 2 mid-year; Gen 3 software to agencies beginning of next year. Fixing 430,000 vehicles could take 1–2 years minimum to complete when including parts and agency agreement; repairs per vehicle might take 5–10 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure vehicles remain safe and legally drivable during process
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether affected vehicles are legal and safe to drive while investigations and remedies proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA stated the cars are legal and safe to drive; executives repeated that owners can legally and safely drive their cars despite emissions noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous technical testing and validation of remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and thoroughly test technical solutions (software/hardware) to ensure they meet emissions standards and do not introduce other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical engineering in Germany must develop/test solutions; testing must validate that fixes meet emissions standards. Example of defeat-device detection: software detecting dyno/testing conditions via steering wheel angle, speed parameters, etc. VW to share technical details with agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental remediation and mitigation of excess pollution
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess health and environmental impacts of excess NOx emissions and propose mitigation measures for harm caused over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members asked what VW will do to rectify excess pollution and health impacts (asthma, respiratory illnesses). VW referenced EPA statements and noted its share of national NOx emissions; mitigation and restitution to be part of discussions with agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve fuel economy (MPG) and minimize performance degradation
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies should aim to maintain published fuel economy (Monroney label) and minimize loss of engine performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Horn stated current understanding is that correcting NOx to standards will allow customers to get Monroney label MPG; there might be slight performance impacts (e.g., 1–2 mph top speed). Any significant differences would prompt compensation discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhaul compliance processes to prevent recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine and reform corporate compliance processes and standards to ensure similar misconduct cannot happen again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW committed to examine compliance processes; Jones Day and internal bodies to recommend process adjustments. Timeline for compliance overhaul was not provided and remains under investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and potential disciplinary or legal action
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, hold accountable, and, if appropriate, subject to legal action the individuals or groups responsible for installing defeat devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations ongoing to identify responsible parties. Witnesses repeatedly asked who authorized or developed the defeat device and where culpability lies (e.g., engineers vs. corporate authorization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing cooperation with regulatory and investigative authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide agencies with requested information and cooperate with investigations, including sharing findings as they become available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executives promised to provide information when they 'find out' and to work with EPA, CARB, NHTSA, and independent investigators; Jones Day retained to manage investigations and interaction with authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer notification scope and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Define which customers will be contacted (e.g., purchasers since model year 2009) and the method of outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW indicated dealers may contact customers dating back to model year 2009 as one possibility; dealers and call centers should be provided scripts, FAQs, and unified messages for outreach.
